title: First professional job at the 401 Ballroom
summary: Charlie Eckels hired him for a dime-a-dance hall at 401 North Main, Los Angeles, at $40 a week with no taxes.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I think I was out of work for about two weeks, when a friend of mine who I'd known through school up in Oakland, by the name of Charlie Eckels, had an orchestra that worked over here in Los Angeles in a place called 401 Ballroom, which was one of the establishments where they usually call these places dime-a-dance parlors.
And that was in Los Angeles?
Yeah, on North Main Street, yes.
I would say that was about '40 -- I mean '27, the early part of '27, very early.
And you were telling me earlier about how much money you made there.
Oh, we made the phenomenal salary of $40.00 a week.
And that was high for that time.
That was nice. That was good. There was no tax. There was nothing, you know, to be taken out. It was just plain -- you didn't even have an income tax or anything.
